title: Genetically higher BMD is associated with higher knee-osteoarthritis risk yet lower fracture risk: pleiotropy-aware Mendelian-randomisation evidence
description: Analysis code, configuration, and reproduction material for the manuscript "Genetically higher BMD is associated with higher knee-osteoarthritis risk yet lower fracture risk: pleiotropy-aware Mendelian-randomisation evidence" (submitted to Osteoarthritis and Cartilage). The repository contains the full Python/R pipeline (LDSC genetic correlation across 78 phenotype pairs, two-sample Mendelian randomisation with MR-Egger / weighted median / MR-PRESSO / leave-one-out, multivariable MR conditioning on adult height and BMI, colocalisation, MRlap sample-overlap correction, and statistical power) and the derived outputs needed to reproduce every table and figure, including the multivariable-MR height/BMI grid and the colocalisation contrast. v2.4 incorporates the M1-M6 adversarial-reviewer rectification: GEFOS variant-level validation confirming the deposited BMD beta is already on the true per-SD scale (no x3.543 reconstruction required), the Systemic Osteogenic Set-point hypothesis restated as a falsifiable hypothesis rather than a demonstrated mechanism, and explicit power caveats for the multivariable-MR height/BMI conditioning and the fracture-versus-knee-OA colocalisation contrast. Raw GWAS summary statistics are not redistributed; they are publicly published (cited in the manuscript) and re-derived by the pipeline.

This re-archive only corrects the Zenodo record metadata (title de-causalised to pleiotropy-aware wording; version/date fixed; M1-M6 plus m1-m10 adversarial-reviewer rectification described): OAC-compliant 3996/4000-word manuscript; GEFOS variant-level scale validation confirming the deposited BMD beta is already on the true per-SD scale (no x3.543 reconstruction required), SOS theory boundary restated as a falsifiable hypothesis, MVMR/colocalisation power caveats. No raw GWAS data are included; all inputs are publicly available and cited in the manuscript.
